To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) simulation based and CNN models of physical scene understanding are both capable of super human performance, 2) simulation based models generalize more broadly to novel situations, 3) simulation based models are more consistent with systematic perceptually based judgment asymmetries, and 4) the two classes of models can be distinguished by their qualitative differences.

(1) Simulation based models can predict human physical judgments in ways that are qualitatively and quantitatively similar to people, but (2) only simulation based models are consistent with human systematic biases and generalizability to novel situations.

simulation based and CNN approaches to physical scene understanding can both achieve super-human accuracy levels and can both quantitatively predict people's physical judgments, but that the simulation based approach can also generalize to novel situations and qualitatively predict systematic perceptual illusions that the CNN approach cannot.
